correctness.rationale: The six prime factorials give a unimodular valuation basis. Factorials 2! through 16! reduce exactly to N^6 together with the two vectors for 14! and 15!, with 16!=15!(2!)^4. Eliminating the two nonnegative coefficients gives the stated necessary-and-sufficient inequalities, and the canonical coefficients reconstruct the original coordinate vector. The packaged exact-integer verifier recomputes every factorial vector and corroborates the elimination on 3,198,720 bounded coordinate vectors and 18,225 generated witnesses.

originality.rationale: Full-text and metadata comparisons distinguish the new fixed-support semigroup theorem from global counting, factorial-decomposition, distinct-factorial, and sequence-table results. The closest prior available finding only identifies the first obstruction and is strictly weaker.

value.rationale: The first failure of the prime-factorial normal form is a natural structural boundary. Closing the entire support-13 layer with an exact semigroup, a valuation inequality, and a canonical representation is a complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice, and it provides a concrete template for subsequent layers.
